title: Geared Deadbolt
description:
A replacement for CRL's declining deadbolt line. The existing design had three problems: the T-turn's orientation let thieves reach it through the door gap, the force needed to lock and unlock grew too high on tall ladder pulls, and it supported only two-point locking.

The concept uses a geared mechanism, building on what CRL learned from a recent three-point locking project, to cut operating force, remove the vulnerable T-turn orientation and support entrances with three or more locking points. It cleared Gate 0 in early 2025.

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: The T-turn could be reached through the door gap; operating force was too high on long ladder pulls; only two-point locking was supported.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: A geared deadbolt that replaces the current mechanism, reduces operating force and expands CRL's multi-point locking category.

brief.label: Customers
brief.text: Architects and Division 8 construction: hotels, government buildings, retail, hospitals, offices, banks, schools and libraries.

brief.label: Value
brief.text: A ladder-pull locking option that is more theft resistant yet still easy to operate at longer pull lengths.

charts.title: Current deadbolt vs geared concept
charts.caption: The three customer problems the concept is designed to solve.
charts.rows:
Locking points | Up to 2 | 3 or more
Thumb-turn | T-turn reachable through the door gap | Re-oriented to remove that path
Operating force on long pulls | High | Reduced by gearing
Market position | Declining sales | Re-establish and grow share

my_role: I co-led the geared deadbolt concept with the senior product manager through Gate 0: defining the field problems with sales and engineering, framing the market, and setting the requirements for an in-house design.
